questions.answer: It was alright, somewhat different from what I'm accustomed to, as I applied for the bachelor's semester program, and the two courses were interconnected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *

A lot more fieldwork and a lot more selfstudy. 
The fieldwork was really good and it was cool to learn in the field. A lot of the other stuff we did was mostly selfstudy.

questions.answer: Longyearbyen is just a gigantic community where everyone knows everyone - a big difference from Copenhagen

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Community

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Save up some money to buy a used snowmobile and/or skis. There's not much to do in the winter (January/February) if you don't have these. However, you can also rent a snowmobile, but this might cost you as much, if not more.
- Don't buy all the cool outdoor gear before you come here. There are excellent outdoor stores, and everything is tax-free.
- Don't make too many plans in advance. The weather changes a lot, and everything is very spontaneous.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a 'shop', where you can get a lot of free stuff (Bedsheets, chlothes, shoes, slippers) so dont worry about packing a lot of things.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, community and nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
- The dark season was difficult but truly beautiful. 
- Since everyone lives in student housing, you don't have much time for yourself.
